panels.title: Containment comes from node_run, never from sla_case

options.content:
`get_or_create_open_case_for_fallback` **requires** an existing OPEN case for the session, so repeated failures inside one session create no new case. Measured: 15 HumanFallback node runs produced only 9 cases — **40% suppression**, all six misses inside a single session. Using `sla_case` as the numerator would report 10.34% escalation instead of the true **17.24%**.

Every handoff and containment number here is therefore computed from `node_run` joined to `node` on `node_type = 'HumanFallback'`. The reconciliation panel below is what makes the suppression visible.

**The contractual SLA numbers are deliberately absent — see the placeholder at the bottom. An SLA-breach alert built today would be permanently silent.**

targets.rawSql:
with runs as (
  select fr.flow_run_id
  from flow_run fr
  join session s on s.session_id = fr.session_id
  where $__timeFilter(fr.created_at)
    and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or s.tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
),
fallbacks as (
  select distinct nr.flow_run_id
  from node_run nr
  join node n on n.node_id = nr.node_id
  where n.node_type = 'HumanFallback'
    and nr.flow_run_id in (select flow_run_id from runs)
)
select
  (select count(*) from fallbacks)::numeric / nullif((select count(*) from runs), 0) as "handoff rate",
  1 - (select count(*) from fallbacks)::numeric / nullif((select count(*) from runs), 0) as "containment"

panels.title: sla_case vs HumanFallback reconciliation
panels.description: The check that makes the 40% dedupe suppression detectable and localises it to a cohort. A day where fallbacks exceed cases is a day where users hit a dead end repeatedly inside one session with no new case opened.

targets.rawSql:
with fallbacks as (
  select date_trunc('day', nr.created_at) as day, count(*) as fallback_node_runs
  from node_run nr
  join node n on n.node_id = nr.node_id
  join flow_run fr on fr.flow_run_id = nr.flow_run_id
  join session s on s.session_id = fr.session_id
  where n.node_type = 'HumanFallback'
    and $__timeFilter(nr.created_at)
    and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or s.tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
  group by 1
),
cases as (
  select date_trunc('day', opened_at) as day, count(*) as sla_cases
  from sla_case
  where $__timeFilter(opened_at)
    and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
  group by 1
)
select
  coalesce(f.day, c.day) as day,
  coalesce(f.fallback_node_runs, 0) as fallback_node_runs,
  coalesce(c.sla_cases, 0) as sla_cases,
  coalesce(f.fallback_node_runs, 0) - coalesce(c.sla_cases, 0) as suppressed
from fallbacks f
full outer join cases c on c.day = f.day
order by day desc

panels.title: Open case backlog by fallback reason
panels.description: Uses ix_sla_case_tenant_status. Deliberately not labelled by priority, which is 0/9 populated.

targets.rawSql:
select status, fallback_reason, count(*) as cases
from sla_case
where $__timeFilter(opened_at) and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
group by status, fallback_reason
order by cases desc

panels.title: Open case age
panels.description: The only breach-adjacent signal obtainable without a policy or an evaluator. The oldest open case is currently 132 days old.

targets.rawSql:
select
  sla_case_id::text as sla_case_id,
  fallback_reason,
  opened_at,
  round(extract(epoch from (now() - opened_at))::numeric, 0) as age_seconds
from sla_case
where $__timeFilter(opened_at) and status = 'OPEN'
  and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
order by opened_at
limit 100

panels.title: Handoff reason mix
panels.description: Only 4 of 10 SLAFallbackReason values have an emitter (POLICY_BLOCK, TOOL_FAILURE, UNKNOWN_INTENT, LOW_CONFIDENCE). USER_REQUESTED_HUMAN, USER_FRUSTRATION and TIMEOUT are unreachable, so this mix cannot distinguish a customer asking for a human (healthy) from the bot failing (unhealthy).

targets.rawSql:
select fallback_reason as metric, count(*) as value
from sla_case
where $__timeFilter(opened_at)
  and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
group by fallback_reason
order by value desc

panels.title: Authoring audit by resource type
panels.description: The one governance surface that genuinely works: 1015 rows with justification on every one. A spike in VERSION_PUBLISHED is the leading incident indicator.

targets.rawSql:
select resource_type, event_type, change_type, count(*) as events
from authoring_event
where $__timeFilter(occurred_at)
  and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
group by 1, 2, 3
order by events desc
limit 50

panels.title: Policy authoring blind spot
panels.description: Inverted risk profile: importing a tool is fully audited, while publishing an access-policy version that grants a principal a new scope leaves no trace. Any family showing 0 events is unaudited.

targets.rawSql:
with families(resource_type) as (
  values ('access_policy'), ('billing_policy'), ('execution_limit_policy'), ('memory_policy'),
         ('rag_policy'), ('rate_limit_policy'), ('runtime_policy'), ('ai_execution_policy')
)
select
  f.resource_type,
  count(a.authoring_event_id) as authoring_events,
  case when count(a.authoring_event_id) = 0 then 'UNAUDITED' else 'audited' end as audit_status
from families f
left join authoring_event a
  on a.resource_type = f.resource_type
  and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or a.tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
group by f.resource_type
order by authoring_events

panels.title: Runtime governance decisions
panels.description: GuardrailChecked is the only runtime governance decision persisted in Postgres. If every row reads ALLOW with limit 'none', that is the misconfiguration described in gap G-10, not a clean bill of health.

targets.rawSql:
select
  ee.type,
  ee.payload->>'decision' as decision,
  ee.payload->>'guardrail_type' as guardrail_type,
  ee.payload->>'model_alias' as model_alias,
  ee.payload->>'limit' as applied_limit,
  count(*) as events
from execution_event ee
where ee.type in ('GuardrailChecked', 'GuardrailBlocked', 'GuardrailDegraded', 'LimitExceeded')
  and $__timeFilter(ee.occurred_at)
  and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or ee.tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
group by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
order by events desc

panels.title: Authoring activity by principal
panels.description: principal_id is safe as a SQL GROUP BY here. It must never become a Prometheus label: user identity is unbounded and would blow the series budget.

targets.rawSql:
select principal_id, resource_type, count(*) as events, max(occurred_at) as last_event
from authoring_event
where $__timeFilter(occurred_at)
  and ('${tenant:csv}' = '$__all' or tenant_id::text = any(string_to_array('${tenant:csv}', ',')))
group by 1, 2
order by events desc
limit 50

panels.title: Not measurable: SLA breach, assignment, resolution, guardrail enforcement

options.content:
These panels are **deliberately absent**. Each would render as a healthy-looking zero forever, which is a worse failure mode than a missing chart.

**SLA breach rate, time to assign, time to resolve, resolution-status mix, escalation level (gap G-07b).** Three independent breaks, all of which must be fixed together:
1. `human_sla_policy` has **0 rows** and `HumanSLAPolicyRepository` exposes no create method; the OpenAPI document's 144 paths contain none matching `human` or `escalation`. So `resolve_policy` returns None and the service explicitly nulls `priority`, `sla_target_at` and `human_sla_policy_id`.
2. **No evaluator runs.** `evaluate_sla` has no caller anywhere in `src` — no scheduler, no cron — and it short-circuits on `human_sla_policy_id is None` regardless.
3. **No case ever leaves OPEN.** `SLAStatus.ABANDONED` is declared and never set.

Measured: `assigned_at`, `resolved_at`, `sla_target_at`, `sla_breached`, `priority`, `human_agent_id`, `resolution_status`, `human_sla_policy_id` are **all 0/9**.

**Guardrail block and degrade rate (gap G-10).** `RuntimePolicyLlmSchema` declares no cost field at any scope, so Pydantic **silently drops** `max_cost_usd`, `max_cost_usd_per_flow_run`, `max_llm_calls_per_flow_run` and friends before they reach the engine. Every cost branch is guarded by `if max_cost_flow is not None` and is therefore unreachable. Fixing the Redis counters or the 1000x pricing bug would not make a single guardrail fire — the schema addition is the unlock.

**Rate-limit and access-policy denial rate (gap G-12).** Recorded nowhere: not Postgres, not Redis, not logs. The rate-limit raise sits outside both tracer spans, and the span on that path is even recorded as a **success** immediately before returning 403.
